name: Palacio Episcopal, Salamanca (Franco HQ 1936–37)
story: After his investiture as head of state, Franco moved his headquarters to Salamanca, installing himself in the bishop's palace beside the cathedrals, lent by Bishop Enrique Pla y Deniel — whose 1936 pastoral 'Las dos ciudades' framed the war as a crusade. From here Franco directed the attack on Madrid, the war in the North and the unification of Falange and Carlists (April 1937). German and Italian envoys and the press office operated nearby, making Salamanca the rebel zone's working capital until the move to Burgos. In October 1936 the nearby University hall saw Unamuno's famous clash with General Millán-Astray.
see: The palace facade on Plaza Juan XXIII next to the New Cathedral; since 2023 it houses the Museo Diocesano (Fernando Gallego paintings and sacred art).
plan: Museum opening hours and ticket apply; exterior free. Easily combined with the Centro Documental de la Memoria Histórica five minutes away.
